sites.name: Camp George West Military Training Complex

overview: Camp George West is a documented military training complex near Golden with a surviving historic campus and major National Guard-era training resources.

sites.category: WWII Ordnance Plant / Federal Industrial Complex
overview: The Denver Federal Center preserves the campus identity of the World War II Denver Ordnance Plant, a major military-industrial manufacturing complex.

overview: Air Force Plant PJKS in the Waterton area was a Cold War missile-test complex associated with Glenn L. Martin and Titan development, with documented test-facility remnants.

sites.name: Leyden Coal Mine, Company Town & Railroad Complex

overview: Leyden was a coal-mining complex with a company town and railroad connection; surviving camp fabric identifies the broader industrial landscape.

sites.name: Lookout Mountain Lariat Trail & Denver Mountain Parks Road Complex
sites.category: Historic Scenic Road / Park Infrastructure Complex
overview: The Lariat Trail is a historic scenic road and Denver Mountain Parks corridor whose surviving alignment and infrastructure define the Lookout Mountain landscape.

sites.name: Morrison Stone, Lime & Town Company Quarry and Industrial Town Landscape
sites.category: Quarry / Industrial Company Town / Railroad Landscape
overview: The Morrison Stone, Lime & Town Company quarry shaped an industrial company-town and railroad landscape whose surviving features identify Morrison's stone-working history.

sites.name: Mount Falcon Walker Estate & Summer White House Ruins Complex

sites.name: Red Rocks Park & Mount Morrison CCC–WPA Complex

overview: Red Rocks Park is a nationally significant New Deal landscape whose amphitheatre, Civilian Conservation Corps camp resources, and park infrastructure identify the broader CCC–WPA complex.

sites.name: Rocky Flats Nuclear Weapons Plant & Cleanup Landscape
sites.category: Cold War Nuclear Weapons / Industrial Archaeology Complex
overview: Rocky Flats was a major Cold War nuclear-weapons production plant; its documented former industrial footprint and cleanup landscape identify the historic complex.

sites.name: Schwartzwalder Mine & Ralston Buttes Uranium Complex
sites.category: Uranium Mine / Mining District / Remediation Complex
overview: The Schwartzwalder Mine anchors the Ralston Buttes uranium complex, identified by its documented production history, mine workings, and remediation landscape.

sites.name: Bankers Lode Claim
overview: Bankers Lode Claim is a historic underground mining property in Jefferson County's Ralston Buttes mining district, developed along a north-trending breccia zone in Precambrian crystalline rock.
timeline: The mine was developed with a drift about 500 feet long, two raises, and a crosscut; later published descriptions reported the workings as extensively collapsed.
In 1954, federal uranium-reconnaissance work included a preliminary report and geologic map of the Bankers Lode workings in the district.
moreHistory: Published geologic descriptions place the Bankers Lode Claim in the SE quarter of the NW quarter of section 9, Township 2 South, Range 71 West, at roughly 8,500 feet elevation. Reported mineralization includes fluorite and copper minerals such as chalcocite, with secondary malachite and cuprite among the noted minerals.
